utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session now again. You were asking about a decision about two documents in relation to the expert witness, Zecevic. You were asking questions about the quality of some 92 bis documents, and you asked about a BH Army document in relation to which you wrote a letter to Mr. Ierace. These are just short, the issues you raised. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to the tender of the material from Mr. Zecevic, that is being handled by Mr. Stamp. I think the last development was that you required some further discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that question was addressed to us. We have -- we have asked the parties to write down a few lines on the issue. And I would have -- if Mr. Stamp would be available, I would have one or two short questions to him in respect of that. So if we could deal with that perhaps later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I respectfully suggest towards the end of the day, Mr. President? There are some constraints on the availability of Witness Y.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it can be done in two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: 92 bis, there were some requirements specified by you late last week, which we will attend to. And in relation to the letter, I will reply to the letter today so that my learned colleague receives a faxed reply this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you first wait what the reply is. It is better than to speculate on it at this very moment. Then, if the Prosecution would be ready to -- yes, Mr. -- this seems to be magic words. If I ask one of the parties whether they are ready --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you know how words can be magic. The other problem which can be raised, Mr. President: Wednesday, we should hear a witness, that I believe that I can name him -- I am just going to check. This is Witness Fraser, and this witness now completely disappeared from the list. He doesn't seem to be on the list of the Prosecution. It would be useful if the Defence could know when is this witness who is supposed to come up on Friday and was not able to be heard, when is he going to be called to the witness box. We haven't had any message on this issue and we think that -- we thought that he would be on Monday, so we prepared, in essence, for this witness. But, of course, it is with great pleasure that we will hear Witness Y, who is going to be appearing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Fraser was to have been called last Friday but, for obvious reasons, could not. Mr. Piletta-Zanin raised this issue with me before court and I told him that we could call Mr. Fraser after Mr. Mole and before Mr. Bergeron.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The matter was raised before and you got an answer, Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I had just an element of an answer because what I wanted to know is what day exactly, for reasons of flights. You could see that last Friday I had a problem. I was given an estimated answer. So could I be given an answer in writing as soon as the witness can be specified for which day? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the answer you got was not complete, you could have asked for completion of the answer. Mr. Ierace, may I take it that the Prosecution is ready to call its next witness? Yes. And I think we first should turn into closed session, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are we in closed session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of July, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
